item.title: #3601421: Docker group restart fails on Ubuntu 26.04: no sg or newgrp
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +121/−17 · bats +67/−2 · sh +54/−15
  • Diff: 14adf9c
  • Discussion: #3601421 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The One Line Installer no longer dies on Ubuntu 26.04 after installing Docker Engine. That release ships neither sg nor newgrp, so the new docker group membership could not be activated, and the installer waited 60 seconds for a Docker daemon it could not reach before failing. It now restarts itself with sudo -u "$USER" -g docker when sg is missing, so the install carries on. If neither works, it stops immediately with log-out advice instead of waiting.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In linux_ensure_docker, a new _docker_group_activator helper prints sg if available, else sudo, else nothing. sg remains the first choice. _reexec_under_docker_group now takes sg or sudo as an argument. With no activator, the installer calls die right away, skipping the 60 s wait. The message no longer mentions newgrp.

The sudo path builds its command in _docker_group_sudo_argv, which fills the DOCKER_GROUP_SUDO_ARGV array. It runs sudo -u "$USER" -g docker env ... bash <installer> <original args>. The issue notes that sudo-rs (the sudo on Ubuntu 26.04) ignores -E and drops variables such as INSTALLER_URL, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and WAYLAND_DISPLAY. So every exported variable (compgen -e) is passed back through env VAR=value. OLI_DOCKER_GROUP_REEXEC is excluded from that list and set to 1 explicitly, so the re-exec guard still prevents looping. New bats tests cover sg present, sg missing with sudo, neither available, and the argv construction.

item.title: #3586418: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Image-and-Audio-to-Video Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +1531/−166 · php +1213/−166 · css +162 · js +147 · yml +9
  • Diff: 3e3231e
  • Discussion: #3586418 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

The Image and Audio to Video explorer in ai_api_explorer is rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. Image and audio now come from the shared file picker (upload, recent runs or media library). An Output box shows the video's shape (from the image) and length (from the audio) before you run. Each run is stored as a run card with the video player, the input image and audio, a download button and a generated PHP code example. Provider and model selection now use the ai_provider_configuration form element. The old bugs are gone: the model was read from a form key that did not match the form prefix, and the returned VideoFile array was passed to a function that expected a single value, which showed as 'Configuration Error'.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ImageAndAudioToVideoGenerator was rewritten around the base-plugin helpers: buildLayout(), providerElement('image_and_audio_to_video', ...), executeRun(), buildRunResults() and resultsResponse(). Inputs are two ai_api_explorer_file elements (#media_type of image and audio). They are converted with ExplorerFile::toOperationFile() and passed to ImageAndAudioToVideoInput. The old AiProviderFormHelper, ExplorerOutputFiles and FileUrlGeneratorInterface constructor dependencies are removed.

Every video in the provider response is saved as a file attached to the run. Its MIME type is taken from the response, then the file name extension, then finfo sniffing, and falls back to video/mp4, so providers that send application/octet-stream still work. Run output stores the image size, the audio name and the video list. Errors such as a missing file, a non-image or non-audio file, or an empty provider response are thrown as translated RuntimeExceptions and shown on the run card. The code example is built with CodeExample in buildRunCode().

A new explorer.image_and_audio_to_video library adds css/explorers/image_and_audio_to_video.css and js/explorers/image_and_audio_to_video.js. The script has two behaviors. aieIavPicker fills the Output shape and length lines from the picker preview. aieIavVideo sizes the video box from the loaded video metadata and pauses other media when one starts. The test module gains a TestImageAndAudioToVideoProvider provider and a sample.mp4 asset, plus FunctionalJavascript tests.

item.title: #3586540: Add optional prompt to ImageToVideoInput and clean up the class
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +53/−11 · php +53/−11
  • Diff: 23fa39b
  • Discussion: #3586540 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

The image_to_video operation type can now carry an optional text prompt. Prompt-guided image-to-video models (the issue names CogVideoX-I2V, LTX-Video, Kling, Runway Gen-3) need a prompt to direct motion, and there was previously no way to pass one. Image-only models are unaffected because the prompt defaults to empty.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ImageToVideoInput::getPrompt() and setPrompt() added; toArray() now returns a prompt key.

Technical details

ImageToVideoInput gains a nullable private $prompt (default NULL) with getPrompt(): ?string and setPrompt(?string): void, mirroring ImageToImageInput. toArray() now includes a prompt key alongside file. The constructor is unchanged (__construct(ImageFile $file)), so existing callers keep working. Providers that support prompts should read $input->getPrompt() and handle NULL.

The same commit fixes copy-pasted audio-to-audio docblocks in ImageToVideoInput and ImageToVideoOutput, and corrects the @param namespace in ImageToVideoInterface to \Drupal\ai\OperationType\ImageToVideo\ImageToVideoInput. ImageToVideoInputTest gets a testPrompt() case.

Upgrade

Providers implementing image_to_video can pass the prompt to the model:

$prompt = $input->getPrompt();

Callers can set it with $input->setPrompt('a cat playing the piano');.

item.title: #3601402: launch_site always opens a browser: an is_drupal:false project with no launch_path lands on a 403
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +171/−17 · bats +123/−1 · sh +44/−12 · md +4/−4
  • Diff: 44d7431
  • Discussion: #3601402 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

When a config sets is_drupal: false and names no launch_path, the installer no longer opens a browser at the end of the run. Before, it opened the empty docroot, which returned a 403, right under the 'Your project is ready' message. The final summary also stops suggesting ddev launch in that case. Drupal builds, and non-Drupal builds that set a launch path such as :6006, behave as before.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: launch_path empty with is_drupal: false (and no LAUNCH_PATH in .ddev/.env) now means no browser launch instead of opening the project root.

Technical details

step_launch_site was the only step that never consulted IS_DRUPAL. A new helper, _launch_site_has_target in launch_site.sh, returns true when IS_DRUPAL is true (or unset) or when _resolve_launch_path returns a non-empty value. _resolve_launch_path already prefers a LAUNCH_PATH line in .ddev/.env over the config value, so a hook that writes that line still triggers the launch. An empty-valued .env line counts as no target.

When there is no target, step_launch_site prints is_drupal=false and no launch_path — nothing to open. and returns 0, so the pipeline continues to agent_handoff. print_welcome calls the same helper. In the no-target case it omits the ddev launch handy-command line and the 'run ddev launch' next step. If an agent is configured, it prints 'start building with ddev <agent>' instead. The issue's alternative of an explicit launch: false key was not implemented. Docs (AGENTS.md-style config reference and the launch_path table entry) and bats tests were updated.

item.title: #3586779: Apply unified UX/design to Decision Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +5280/−618 · php +3114/−615 · js +1280 · css +839 · md +38/−3 · yml +9
  • Diff: 496cad3
  • Discussion: #3586779 · 1 contributor · 19 comments

Summary

The Decision Explorer, the admin page in ai_api_explorer for trying decision calls, is rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. The state can be entered as named fields or JSON. Questions appear as cards instead of a JSON text box. The page lists what the questions need from the model. Answers show as charts, and a box answer is drawn on each uploaded image. Export JSON saves the form, and Import JSON loads a saved form or run back in. A run can be edited and run again.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change is mostly in DecisionGenerator.php, with new js/explorers/decision.js and css/explorers/decision.css files. A new explorer.decision library is declared in the module's libraries file, depending on ai_api_explorer/explorer_ui and ai_api_explorer/media. Per the existing comment in that file, AiApiExplorerPluginBase::buildLayout() attaches only this explorer's own assets. The explorer keeps the ai_provider_configuration element, so only models declaring the features the parsed request needs are listed, and the selected model's features and limits are shown. Incompatible selections and entered criteria are kept for correction.

A refused question is labelled "Refused" and shows no distribution. A box question needs an image. The box is drawn over each image with its edges in pixels.

The export format builds on DecisionInput::toArray(). It has format set to ai_api_explorer_decision, version, title, input (state, questions, files), and optional settings and response. Import also accepts any JSON with state and questions. Exported runs list images by name only, and the form export leaves images out. An image can be included by adding base64, plain or as a data URL. Imported images must be PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP and at most 10 MB. settings is applied only if "Also use the model saved in the file" is checked, and response is ignored. The diff also adds functional JavaScript and kernel tests, including one for editing a run to restore its input. I could not read the PHP and JS diffs, which were omitted from the diff I received. Details of the code are taken from the issue, the docs and CSS diffs, and the test code.

item.title: #3586841: Forward Port from `1.x` to `2.x`
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 336 files, +21418/−12228 · php +19292/−6092 · md +1901/−97 · txt +105/−98 · yml +82/−485 · json +38/−4641 · gitignore +0/−2 · nvmrc +0/−1 · css +0/−68 · svg +0/−11 · js +0/−725 · sh +0/−8
  • Diff: 93e3970
  • Discussion: #3586841 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

This forward-ports features that had landed in 1.x to 2.x. The main addition is a Decision operation type: calling code asks true/false (noul), choice, score and box questions about shared text or structured state, optionally with images, and gets back probabilities and confidence it can threshold on. A default Decision provider can be chosen in AI settings, and an installed provider has to implement it. Guardrails (RegEx, Input Length Limit, Moderation) can run on Decision requests, the API Explorer gains a Decision Explorer, and AI Automators gain boolean, list and numeric field rules backed by Decision. Provider selection forms can now filter models by required capabilities and show what the selected model supports.

The commit also contains documentation and tooling updates. Only 21 of the 336 changed files were visible in the diff I was given, so this summary covers what those files and their docs describe.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: ai.settings default operation providers schema gains a decision entry ('Default decision provider').
  • New API: New decision operation type (DecisionInterface, DecisionInput, DecisionResponse, Drupal\ai\OperationType\Decision\Value question/answer classes), DecisionGuardrailInterface, and optional validate{OperationName}Input() provider hooks.

Technical details

Decision calls go through decision(DecisionInput $input, $model_id, $tags) on a provider and return a normalized DecisionResponse with typed getters (getNoul(), getChoice(), getScore(), getBox()). Helpers are isLikely() for noul and isConfident() for choice, score and box. Question state must be plain arrays, JSON scalars and NULL; objects, resources, non-finite numbers and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. Invalid or incomplete provider answers raise AiBrokenOutputException. Choice and score answers are validated for probability totals, winner and weighted score, with an optional AnswerPrecision for providers that round values for transport. Without it the documented tolerance is 0.02. Box answers expose toPixels(), which rounds outward.

Guardrails: services.yml registers GuardrailExecutionContext, OperationGuardrailHandlerRegistry (a service_collector for the ai.guardrail_operation_handler tag), ChatGuardrailHandler, DecisionGuardrailRunner and DecisionValidationEventSubscriber. Only plugins implementing DecisionGuardrailInterface and declaring supportsOperation('decision', $phase) run on Decision requests, returning PassResult or StopResult. Reaching a set's threshold throws AiDecisionBlockedException, which extends AiUnsafePromptException. Per the docs, global sets attach at priority 100, validation runs at 20 and the guardrail handler at 10. Token-based length limits and similar unsupported checks in a caller-attached set raise AiSetupFailureException; in global sets they are skipped with a warning.

Operation types gain an optional input validator: ProviderProxy calls validate{OperationName}Input(Input $input, string $model_id): void on the configured provider before PreGenerateResponseEvent, so guardrails never see rejected input. The scaffolding skill docs and check script were updated to enforce the exact name and signature. ai_modules_installed() and a new ai_modules_uninstalled() now clear the ai_operation_types discovery cache.

The ai_provider_configuration element gets #capabilities, #show_capabilities and #capability_details_callback, and returns a use_default key. It lists only models declaring every required capability. A current selection that no longer qualifies stays visible, marked incompatible or unavailable. The selection is validated on submit. AiProviderPluginManager::getModelsWithCapabilities() applies the same rule outside forms.

Upgrade

Providers that want to reject bad input early can add a validator named exactly after the operation type, for example:

public function validateChatInput(ChatInput $input, string $model_id): void {
  // Throw AiBadRequestException when the input cannot be handled.
}

Code using ai_provider_configuration should read the new use_default key and resolve the site default when it is TRUE, for example with getDefaultProviderForOperationType().

item.title: #3594888: Filter traces by groups of tags, with AND between groups
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +1157/−164 · php +1089/−155 · css +66/−9 · txt +2
  • Diff: 84d13e7
  • Discussion: #3594888 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The trace review filter in AI Eval now groups tags by the part before the first colon (for example feedback:negative goes under "feedback"; tags without a colon go under "Other"). Ticks inside a group are OR, and different groups are AND, so you can ask for "thumbs down AND not yet labeled" or "this agent AND no answer". Three non-tag filters were added: Source (AI Answers or Imported), Visitor "not rated" (no feedback: tag), and Verdict (unlabeled, pass, fail, deferred). The whole filter now travels in the URL through the list, pager, group links, previous/next and saving a verdict, so a filtered queue can be bookmarked or shared. The failure rates on the review page use the same filter. Group cards and trace cards also show thumbs up/down badges for visitor feedback.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New query parameters on the trace review pages: source[], verdict[], not_rated, alongside from, to and tags[].
  • New API: GroupedTraceSourceInterface gains availableTagGroups() and hasFeedbackTags(); new TraceFilter service class with groupTags() and apply(); TraceSourceInterface filters accept source, not_rated and verdict.

Technical details

The filter logic is centralized in a new Drupal\ai_eval\Service\TraceFilter. groupTags() splits on the first colon (unprefixed goes to other). apply() adds from/to bounds, a source condition on t.span_id LIKE 'ai_answers:%' (selecting both sources adds no constraint), one correlated EXISTS on ai_eval_trace_tag per tag group (OR inside via IN, AND between groups), and a verdict condition. not_rated is OR-ed with any selected feedback:* tags instead of being AND-ed, since it could never match them otherwise. The verdict filter matches the group verdict shown on the card: the earliest group-scope row in ai_eval_review_label (MIN(id)) keyed by TraceFilter::GROUP_KEY_EXPRESSION; unlabeled means no group-scope label exists.

TraceSourceInterface documents the new source, not_rated and verdict keys. GroupedTraceSourceInterface adds availableTagGroups() and hasFeedbackTags(). The DB trace source's groupKeysWithTags() became groupKeysWithFilters(), which uses TraceFilter. TraceReviewController::filtersFromRequest() validates source, verdict (including defer) and not_rated against allow lists. A new filterQuery() serializes the full state into the list, pager, groupUrl(), back link and the verdict save URL. groupNeighbors() is computed before saving a verdict so prev/next stays based on the pre-save filtered set. ratesForReviewedTraces() is now called with the full $filters array instead of just the tags.

The landing route now returns only the #ai-eval-review-landing container as an htmx fragment (HX-Request: true), so filter bar, group list and rates swap together. The filter bar and pager target this container. The filter bar is rebuilt as grouped fieldsets with friendly tag labels, and a collapsible "Other tags" section when it has more than 8 tags. CSS and a spelling dictionary were updated.

Upgrade

Custom implementations of GroupedTraceSourceInterface need the two new methods:

public function availableTagGroups(): array;
public function hasFeedbackTags(): bool;

Code calling ratesForReviewedTraces() with a tag list should pass a filters array instead, e.g. ['tags' => $tags], as TraceReviewController::landing() now passes $filters.

item.title: #3586407: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Tools Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +2723/−242 · php +2099/−242 · css +511 · js +104 · yml +9
  • Diff: 36e5ebe
  • Discussion: #3586407 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Tools explorer in ai_api_explorer is rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. It lists tools in collapsible groups with a search field. A card shows the picked tool's function name, plugin ID, group and whether it likely only reads or may change the site. Arguments are typed and marked as required, and limits and Run as sit in the same form. Results show structured output as a table, with the raw output one click away. Each run also gets a PHP code example. Tools that may change the site ask for confirmation before they run. The explorer no longer needs a chat provider to open, since tools use no model. Several bugs are fixed: Run as was ignored, tool output was not escaped, and an empty limit value triggered PHP warnings.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ToolsExplorer::isActive() now returns TRUE, so the explorer no longer depends on the chat operation type. The hub card shows the tool count via getHubSummary(). The form is built from the shared shell and components, with explorer-specific files attached through a new explorer.tools library in ai_api_explorer.libraries.yml (css/explorers/tools.css, js/explorers/tools.js). The JS handles tool search, "Show more" for long groups, and "Show all N rows" for long output tables. The table/raw switch is the shared ExplorerUi::viewSwitch().

Runs go through executeRun(), so they are stored with the run history when it is enabled and the explorer still works with it off. Each run records the function name, group and who it ran as. Run as is now applied: runAsAccount() switches with the injected AccountSwitcherInterface and switches back in a finally block. Role options in runAsOptions() are limited to the current user's own roles plus anonymous and authenticated, and only roles whose permissions are a subset of the user's. Users with administer permissions may pick any such role. The switched session keeps the current user ID via runAsUid() (user 1 uses 0), so "edit own" permissions do not match content owned by anonymous. Access-denied results are detected from exception messages and from status: access_denied in action tool output, and are shown as access errors.

Argument and limit validation failures are stored as failed runs with a Retry action, not form errors. limitConstraints() rejects a limit with no values with a message instead of calling explode() on NULL. Output goes through Html::escape() in the table cells and raw <pre> view. Read versus write is a guess from the tool's group: READ_GROUPS (information_tools, context_tools) run immediately, and WRITE_GROUPS need a confirm checkbox. A test tool plugin ai_api_explorer_test:list_colors and Functional and FunctionalJavascript tests were added. SetupNeededTest now expects no setup screen for this explorer.

item.title: #3586781: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Extractive Question Answering Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +1065/−158 · php +878/−157 · css +114 · js +63 · yml +9 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 1ddacf4
  • Discussion: #3586781 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

The Extractive Question Answering Explorer in AI API Explorer has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. The answer is now highlighted inside the passage instead of being shown as a table of start and end offsets. When the model returns several candidate answers, you can click one to see where it sits in the passage. The explorer's route is now /admin/config/ai/explorers/extractive_question_answering_generator. Each run is stored through the run history, and its code example is generated per run with escaped values.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The explorer's provider/model selection now uses the ai_provider_configuration form element instead of AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm().

Technical details

ExtractiveQuestionAnsweringGenerator now builds the form with buildLayout() and providerElement('extractive_question_answering', ...). Submission goes through executeRun(), which stores question, context and provider as run input and the sorted answers (answer, score, start, end) as run output. getResponse() returns resultsResponse(), and buildRunOutput() renders the stored run. Answers are sorted by score, best first, and answers without a score go last. Blank answers are dropped.

locateAnswer() decides where an answer sits in the passage. It trusts the offsets as character offsets when the text at that position matches the answer. Otherwise it tries them as byte offsets, then searches for the answer text, and finally falls back to offsets that fit within the passage. Providers that return no offsets still get a highlight when the answer text is found. CRLF line breaks are normalised for display, so the data-start and data-end values on each candidate button match what the browser shows.

The new js/explorers/extractive_question_answering.js behavior moves the <mark> when a candidate button is clicked. It splits the passage by code point so the offsets stay consistent with PHP's mb_* functions. The buttons use aria-pressed, and the range text sits in an aria-live region. Styles are in css/explorers/extractive_question_answering.css and are attached through the new explorer.extractive_question_answering library.

The code example is built with the shared CodeExample builder, replacing the hand-built HTML string that pasted the question and passage in unescaped. The passage and answers are escaped with Html::escape(). The diff also adds a ai_api_explorer_test provider plugin (TestExtractiveQaProvider), a functional test and a docs URL update.

item.title: #3586416: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Speech-To-Speech Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +1705/−197 · php +1544/−193 · css +105 · js +42 · yml +9 · md +5/−4
  • Diff: dd45512
  • Discussion: #3586416 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Speech to Speech Explorer in the AI API Explorer module is rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. It now offers two tasks, Change voice and Translate speech, and takes the recording through the shared file picker. Results are stored as runs, with the original shown next to the result. The explorer previously could not run because provider and model always came through as NULL. That is fixed. Saved result files now get an extension and MIME type that match the actual audio format.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

SpeechToSpeechGenerator is rewritten on AiApiExplorerPluginBase::buildLayout(). Provider and model selection moves to the ai_provider_configuration element via providerElement(), replacing AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm(). The old bug came from a form prefix sts while submit read speech_to_speech keys. Submit now reads the provider element value and resolves it with resolveProviderValue().

The operation takes only the recording, so voice, target language and output format are provider configuration. processOptions() fills the voice, language and format fields from the selected model's configuration, looking for keys such as voice/voice_id, target_language/target_lang/language and output_format/response_format/format. runConfiguration() passes only the setting of the chosen task: a voice change sends no language, a translation sends no voice (covered by the new unit test SpeechToSpeechConfigurationTest). A new explorer.speech_to_speech library holds speech_to_speech.css and speech_to_speech.js. The script shows the settings and run button of the picked task, because #states does not apply to AJAX-replaced content.

The saved file type is now chosen by audioType(). It checks the sniffed bytes first, then the requested format, then the reported MIME type, then the file name. Its comment notes that ElevenLabs reports every result as audio/mpeg. The run is stored through executeRun() with the original and result file details, plus transcript, translation and source/target language when the provider reports them in output metadata. A failed run keeps its error next to its card. The speech_to_speech_generator plugin ID is unchanged, and the title is now 'Speech to Speech Explorer'. The developer docs example now uses audio/mpeg and getNormalized()[0], and the explorer path in the docs is updated.

item.title: #3586712: Require drupal/ai 1.4.11 or later on 1.4, or 1.5.2 or later
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +14/−6 · md +13/−5 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 7cf5aed
  • Discussion: #3586712 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

AI Context now requires a drupal/ai version that shows tooltips as plain text: 1.4.11 or later on the 1.4 branch, or 1.5.2 or later. Older drupal/ai versions (1.4.10 and earlier, 1.5.0, 1.5.1) insert tooltip values as HTML, so HTML stored in a long context item Description or an AI agent description could run as script in an administrator's session when they open the consumer pages. Composer now blocks those versions. Exploiting it needs a privileged permission such as Create AI Context Item or Administer AI Agent.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Stored XSS in admin consumer pages (context item Description and AI agent description tooltips) when drupal/ai renders data-ai-tooltip via innerHTML; requires privileged authors, runs in an administrator's session.
  • Requirements: drupal/ai constraint changed from ^1.4 || ^2 to ~1.4.11 || ^1.5.2 || ^2.

Technical details

CCC puts text in data-ai-tooltip attributes, and the ai/ai_global.js behavior from drupal/ai reads it via dataset.aiTooltip. Two tooltips are escaped once on the CCC side (AiContextItem::buildDescriptionRenderArray() and AiContextConsumersForm::getTruncatedDescription()), which is correct only if drupal/ai uses textContent. With innerHTML the decoded value is parsed as HTML. The commit changes no PHP, Twig or tests: it only changes the composer.json constraint and the version text in README.md, docs/index.md, docs/upgrade-policy.md and docs/features/consumer_configuration.md. The Automator notes now say 1.5.2 instead of 1.5.0.

The constraint deliberately avoids ^1.4.11, because that would allow 1.5.0 and 1.5.1. Composer cannot check the commit of a dev branch, so sites on a drupal/ai dev branch (including all drupal/ai 2 sites, as 2.x has no release yet) must update to the current branch head. The docs say this. Until the follow-up #3586705 lands, some other tooltips (scope pills, +N overflow, Automator description) show HTML entities such as & with these drupal/ai versions, as stated in the issue.

Upgrade

Update drupal/ai together with CCC:

composer update drupal/ai_context drupal/ai -W
drush updatedb

To stay on AI 1.4:

composer update drupal/ai_context drupal/ai -W --with drupal/ai:~1.4.11

If you use a drupal/ai dev branch (for example 1.5.x-dev or 2.x-dev), update it to the current branch head.

Summary

The Rerank Explorer in the AI API Explorer module has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. Documents are edited as numbered rows, and a document can now span several lines (separated by a blank line, where before it was one per line). Results show each document's rank, a score bar and how many places it moved. When Top N is set, the documents below it stay visible, dimmed, under a cut line. Provider and model selection now use the ai_provider_configuration form element, runs are stored with run history, and each run gets a generated code example. Several bugs in the old explorer are fixed, including provider-specific guessing of the result shape.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ReRankOutput constructor takes an optional fourth argument $rawOutput; getRawOutput() returns it, falling back to the normalized results when it is NULL.

Technical details

RerankGenerator now extends the run-based explorer flow: submitForm() calls executeRun(), builds a ReRankInput, and stores a ranking (index and score per result) and the normalized response in the run output. readRanking() reads the normalized output as described by ReRankInterface: each result is an array or object with an index and a relevance_score or score. It drops results with an invalid or repeated index, and the document text always comes from the documents that were sent, not from the provider's result. This replaces the per-provider shape guessing. If no result points to a document, the run fails with an error.

rankRows() appends documents the provider did not return as unranked rows under the cut. A Top N equal to or greater than the document count is sent as 0, meaning all. Score bars use the raw score when it is within 0 to 1; otherwise they span the run's lowest to highest score, with a hint shown. Documents are parsed by parseDocuments(), which splits on blank lines. The textarea stays the real form value, so the form works without JavaScript. The new js/explorers/rerank.js shows numbered, growing rows (add, remove, paste splitting, screen reader announcements) and keeps the textarea in sync, and explorer.rerank in the libraries file loads it with css/explorers/rerank.css.

The code example is built per run with the shared CodeExample builder, so the query is no longer HTML-escaped into the PHP. ReRankOutput::getRawOutput() used to return the normalized results. item.title: #3601420: Create the snap Firefox profile before trusting DDEV's local CA on a fresh Linux desktop
item.description:

  • Changes: 4 files, +115/−4 · bats +82 · sh +32/−3 · md +1/−1

Summary

On a fresh Linux desktop where snap Firefox has never been opened, the installer now starts Firefox once in headless mode so it creates its profile. The DDEV local CA is then added to that profile. Before, the CA step found no profile and printed manual import steps. The site then opened in a Firefox that did not trust the CA, and showed "Warning: Potential Security Risk Ahead". macOS is unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change is in src/lib/platform/ensure_local_https.sh. _trust_snap_browsers now calls the new _snap_firefox_first_run before its loop. That function returns early unless snap Firefox is installed, certutil and firefox are on the PATH, and no ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox/*/cert9.db exists yet. Otherwise it runs timeout 60 firefox --headless --screenshot ~/snap/firefox/common/oli-first-run.png about:blank and removes the screenshot. A failure or timeout is ignored. If no store exists afterwards, the existing manual import message is printed. Firefox creates its own default profile, rather than the installer using -CreateProfile or certutil -N.

A new helper, _snap_installed, checks for /snap/bin/<name>. The browser loop now uses it as well as the ~/snap/<name> directory check, because that directory only appears after a snap's first run. An installed but never opened snap Chromium therefore gets the manual import instructions instead of being skipped silently. Bats tests cover the headless run, the screenshot cleanup, an existing profile, a failed first run, missing certutil, macOS and the Chromium case. AGENTS.md was updated to match.
